reference: There is no matching GNU command for the SCM_RIGHTS builtin. Runnable contract expectations come from Bash type/help behavior and the documented scm_doc/version strings in scm.c. Deferred data-path cases specify Python's AF_UNIX sendmsg/recvmsg SCM_RIGHTS interface as the future independent oracle; those operations are not executed here.
coverage: Bash type -t reports scm as a registered builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented verbs and recv-fd checks.
Deferred AF_UNIX pair, listen/connect, descriptor transfer, token/data binding, descriptor-type filters, and peer-credential checks with independent Python socket expectations.
Metadata results are not operation coverage; deferred operations are not passes.
exclusions: No GNU CLI implements this loadable's SCM_RIGHTS API, so no command-parity case is claimed; Python socket is an adapter oracle, not a GNU command and cannot be substituted as fake parity.

Actual scm socket and descriptor operations are deferred under the task's safety instruction. Their expected behavior and the disposable Linux VM or reviewed mock needed to test them are recorded per case.
The suite does not qualify cross-host behavior, real network activity, host credentials, or a physical terminal.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash classifies scm as a builtin, matching the loadable registration contract.
Check the Bash help entry exposes each documented verb and the important recv-fd filters without invoking socket operations.
cases.script:
doc=$(help scm)
if [[ $doc == *'Unix-domain socket FD passing via SCM_RIGHTS.'* &&
      $doc == *'scm pair [-h FDVAR1] [-h FDVAR2]'* &&
      $doc == *'scm listen PATH [-h FDVAR]'* &&
      $doc == *'scm connect PATH [-h FDVAR]'* &&
      $doc == *'scm send-fd SOCK_FD MSG_FD [DATA]'* &&
      $doc == *'scm recv-fd SOCK_FD [-h FDVAR] [-V DATAVAR]'* &&
      $doc == *'--peer-uid UID'* && $doc == *'--token DATA'* &&
      $doc == *'--fd-regular'* ]]; then
  printf 'scm help contract ok\n'
else
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Verify the documented version metadata output without exercising an scm operation.
Check the pair verb creates two usable AF_UNIX datagram endpoints and supports binding their descriptor numbers to shell variables.
Check local datagram bind/connect behavior and the listen path rule that only a stale socket may be removed while a non-socket entry is preserved.
Check send-fd passes a fixture descriptor with SCM_RIGHTS and carries explicit, omitted, and empty DATA bodies according to its documented fallback behavior.
Check recv-fd receives a descriptor, binds its number and message body to requested shell variables, accepts a matching token, and closes the received descriptor on token mismatch.
Check --fd-regular, --fd-socket, and --fd-tty accept matching received descriptors and reject mismatches while closing rejected descriptors.
Check the optional peer UID, GID, and PID filters, including mismatches and malformed numeric arguments.
cases.reason: No executed case. The VM script runs as root, so a python helper can fork, setresgid/setresuid to fixture ids (e.g. 4242/4343) and connect, giving a distinct-identity peer without new driver capability.
